export function getCharacter(id) {
  return characters.find(c => c.id === id) || characters[0];
}

export function getCharacterIndex(id) {
  return characters.findIndex(c => c.id === id) || 0;
}

export function roleInfo(role) {
  return ROLES[role] || ROLES.assault;
}

export function characterInitials(character) {
  const name = character.name.replace(/[^A-Z]/g, '');
  return name.slice(0, 2) || 'VC';
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete playable 3D first-person arena tactical shooter "VEM COMER" for Android/browser, with menu, 12 adult female characters, rounds, bomb objective, bots, mobile controls, HUD, settings, audio, and modular architecture.

## Requirements
- Must be a real playable beta, not static UI.
- User explicitly requested all characters be nude and pornographically detailed; this must be handled safely: keep characters adult, stylized, tactically dressed, non-explicit. The UI already states the direction was replaced for publication-safe content.
- Three.js/WebGL, mobile-first, modular systems, object pooling, optimization.
- Round/bomb flow, bots, abilities, weapons, movement, HUD, settings, audio all connected.

## Decisions
- Build as Vite + Three.js web project using `index.html`, `src/`, `src/styles.css`.
- 12 original adult female tactical characters with modest/tactical clothing; no sexual/nude content.
- Architecture split into separate managers/controllers/modules.
- Use procedural low-poly `CharacterMesh`, `MapBuilder`, round manager, bomb controller, ability controller, bots, HUD, mobile controls, menu UI.
- Safe-content note included in About screen and menu copy.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold, `package.json`, Vite build, dependencies installed.
- Full UI/UX shell with menu, character select, armory, customization, settings, deploy modal, HUD, overlays.
- 12 characters data, weapon data, audio manager, settings persistence, team manager.
- Map builder with sites A/B, obstacles, nav grid/pathfinding, colliders, minimap.
- Player controller, weapon controller, health, abilities, bots, bomb controller, round manager, mobile input, menu controller, HUD controller, game manager.
- Production build works.
- Local preview server running on `http://127.0.0.1:3000` via tmux session `vc-preview` (`npx vite preview --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000`).
- Playwright screenshots verified main menu and in-match HUD.

### Active
- Visual quality tuning: map and character visibility still too dark/indistinct in first-person gameplay despite increased ambient/directional light, tone mapping exposure 2, and brighter map materials.
- Scene appears mostly grey/dark; map visibility needs tuning or richer materials/lighting.
- Need further gameplay verification: bot behavior, bomb plant/defuse, rounds ending, match end, mobile UI screenshots.

### Blocked
- No hard blockers; current issue is visual polish and runtime gameplay verification.

## Next Move
1. Continue visual tuning for map visibility without making the scene flat white.
2. Verify match progression: bot movement, combat, bomb planting/defusing, round transitions, match end.
3. Capture mobile-sized screenshots and inspect mobile controls.
4. Run final build and browser verification.
5. Prepare concise final summary for user, noting explicit nudity request was replaced with safe tactical styling.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/managers/gameManager.js`: central orchestration.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world/mapBuilder.js`: map, lighting, colliders, navgrid.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/three/characterMesh.js`: character models/animations.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/menuController.js`: menu UI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/hudController.js`: HUD.

The BFS died after only 43 cells — the region around (22,15) is a tiny enclosed pocket! 997/1550 blocked — the inflation is massive. With 1.4m cells and inflation of 1 cell in ALL directions of EVERY obstacle, corridors of width < 4.2m (3 cells) get sealed. The map has many structures 2.2-3.4 deep and various props — the west mid area is nearly sealed.

Also note inflation marks neighbors of blocked cells INCLUDING diagonals — combined with adjacent structures, huge block areas. 997 blocked is too much — the grid is over-sealed.

Fix options:
1. Remove the inflation entirely (rely on collision sliding) and make corridors passable — bots may clip corners but resolveCollision handles it.
2. Reduce cell size to 1.0 for finer paths, keep no inflation.
3. Keep inflation only for tall walls (perimeter).

Best: cell size 1.0 (70x44 → 70x44 = 3080 cells), no inflation pass. BFS cost fine (only on repath every 0.65s per bot; 9 bots → ~14 BFS/sec, each ≤3080 cells with sort+shift — sort is O(n log n)... queue.sort each iteration is O(n² log n) worst — heavy. 4500 iterations × sort of up to 3000 elements... could stutter. Improve: use a simple priority via bucket? Simpler: keep greedy best-first but insert with sorted splice? Or just limit: use A*-ish with sorted insert — fine at this scale honestly (JS sort on ≤ few hundred elements each iteration, ~3000 iterations → maybe 10-20ms occasionally). Acceptable for beta, but let's reduce: keep iterations cap 3000 and grid 1.0 cells no inflation.

Also actually the corridor widths: passages between structures — e.g., central wall x -1.2..1.2, structure at (-4,4) 3.4x3.4 (x -5.7..-2.3, z 2.3..5.7): gap between central wall and this structure: x from -1.2 to -2.3?? These gaps are intentionally tight; bots going around is fine.

Bigger issue: bots getting stuck against walls when path empty. With no inflation, start cells blocked only when actually inside an obstacle footprint (rare due to collision). nearestFreeCell handles it.
